chapter: Marriage, family and the Capitol albums
title: What a full orchestra feels like
summary: She says singing in front of a symphony orchestra is her favorite thing, though she mostly worked with trios or big bands.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: The arranger on the first two albums was Billy May.

I don’t know if this is a fair question, because this is what people who aren’t singers just want to know: what does it feel like to hear and feel an orchestra behind you, beneath you, an arrangement?

Oh that’s still my favorite. My favorite thing is a full orchestra, symphony orchestra. One of the dreams as a kid was to be standing on a mountaintop with a symphony orchestra behind me, the wind blowing my hair. That was – there’s nothing – nothing could take the place of that. That’s unique and beautiful. As much as I love working with a rhythm section – you notice that through the years I’ve either worked with a big band or three pieces. I have never really – except for Cannonball, I’ve never worked with quintets. Give me the three, just the basics, or give me all of it. And there’s nothing like hearing that full orchestra behind me.
Does it change your – the performance?

I have no idea. It just makes me feel good inside to hear the band. I don’t know that it changes what I sing, because I’m pretty sure that’s pretty much – that’s the same, but it’s just what it does for me to hear that full orchestra. It doesn’t – I would like to be in the audience, watching, sometimes, especially when you have one of those great orchestras. I would love to be one of those people sitting in the seats, to see it.
